title: Taiwan Travelogue
author: Yang Shuang-zi
review: I first knew of this book from Fuchsia Dunlop's post on Instagram. Read and finished it when I was Brussels, a few days after it won the International Booker Prize. A very fascinating backstory about the author and her twin sister.

title: Suder
author: Percival Everett
review: The storyline reminds me of the TV series Yellowjackets (don't watch it). The storyline get more and more absurd, and some loose ends don't get fully resolved. It was good to read Everett's first novel to get a sense of how his early interests continue in his other writings. Also got me onto Charlie Parker.

title: Glyph
author: Percival Everett
review: Purchased with Suder. Both copies are signed by the author(!)

title: Baby Boom
author: Yokoyama Yuichi
review: Colours, lines, shapes. Bought in 2025 at the Pagemasters Zine Fair.

title: Baskerville's Teardrop Explodes - A Selection of Books as Muses
author: John Morgan
review: Published posthumously by one of my favourite book designers. The book itself is simple and unassuming, and in my opinion embodies similar qualities of the muses that Morgan had picked.

title: So Much Blue
author: Percival Everett
review: Probably the best of Everett's works I have read so far.

title: This Part Is Silent: A Life Between Cultures
author: SJ Kim
review: Could not finish this. I've since donated it to a community library.

title: Unbound
author: Karel Martens
review: Visual delight from a Dutch master of colours and patterns.

title: Terence Conran's New House Book
author: Terence Conran
review: A gift from a friend after I bought a flat in South London. An older edition with lots of useful information that transcends interior trends.
